question: Summarize the Cold Chain Policy.
answer: Cold chain products must be stored between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius. Any temperature excursion must be recorded within one hour. The required response to an excursion depends on the risk class of the SKU, see [[policy-excursion-response]] and [[policy-lot-hold]].

question: Summarize the Excursion Response Policy.
answer: After a temperature excursion, risk class A SKUs require you to place an immediate lot hold and notify the quality lead. Risk class B SKUs require you to open a quality review within 24 hours. Risk class C SKUs require you to log the excursion with no further action. See [[policy-lot-hold]] for hold mechanics.

question: Summarize the Lot Hold Policy.
answer: A lot hold freezes shipment of a lot. Placing a lot hold is a Tier 3 mutation and needs human approval from an authorized reviewer, see [[policy-hitl-approval]]. Lot identifiers use the format LOT-00000 with five digits.

question: Summarize the Human Approval Policy.
answer: Tier 3 actions such as lot holds and SKU status changes are never executed automatically. They are written as PENDING_APPROVAL and wait for a reviewer to approve or reject. Reviewers must not approve their own requests.

question: Summarize the Product Recall Policy.
answer: A recall is initiated by the quality lead after a confirmed safety defect. All lots of the affected SKU are placed on hold, see [[policy-lot-hold]], and customers are notified within 48 hours.

question: Summarize the Personal Data Policy.
answer: Personal data such as email addresses, phone numbers and social security numbers must be redacted before storage. Raw personal data is never written to logs, caches or audit records. See [[policy-audit-log]].

question: Summarize the Audit Log Policy.
answer: Every agent action is written to a hash chained audit log. Each entry includes the hash of the previous entry so tampering is detectable. Audit entries are scoped by tenant.

question: Summarize the Expiry Handling Policy.
answer: Products within 30 days of expiry are flagged for priority shipping. Expired products must be quarantined, see [[policy-quarantine]].

question: Summarize the Quarantine Policy.
answer: Quarantined stock is physically segregated and labeled QUARANTINE. Release from quarantine requires a quality review.

question: Summarize the Supplier Audit Policy.
answer: Critical suppliers are audited every 12 months. Non critical suppliers are audited every 24 months.

question: Summarize the Returns Policy.
answer: Customer returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery when the seal is intact. Returned cold chain products are never restocked.

question: Summarize the Labeling Policy.
answer: Every unit carries a label with SKU, lot number and expiry date. Labels for cold chain products also show the storage temperature range.
